### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via due_on (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e68ba3a18443a75ded9f83e17202fbbd5e36a64e` — the merge of head `df85ac4baabe5a6974e269419b595a274d306c06` into base `4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e68ba3a18443a75ded9f83e17202fbbd5e36a64e && git checkout e68ba3a18443a75ded9f83e17202fbbd5e36a64e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02 df85ac4baabe5a6974e269419b595a274d306c06 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02 && git merge --no-ff df85ac4baabe5a6974e269419b595a274d306c06

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `df85ac4baabe5a6974e269419b595a274d306c06`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #21255 (body; comments 5942982209, 5943357114, 5944459558, 5944487371); PR #21297 (body, the 6-file list, the GitHub diff against merge base `748b2407`); `packages/spec/src/data/filter-cross-field-comparison-class.ts` and `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` (`applyCrossFieldComparison`, `uncompilableFieldReferenceError`) at the merge base; `having-filter.ts`, `engine.ts`, `registry.ts` and `aggregate-field-type-door.ts` at base and head through `git show`; card #21299; and the head's check-runs, read last. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Refused set at the per-aggregation filter — right, and exact.** `assertAggregationFilterReferencesAreDeclared` hands every plain reference to `crossClassReferenceViolation` with `declaredFieldMeta` on both sides (`type` plus `multiple: true`, the two inputs `crossFieldComparisonVerdict` reads) and refuses only the `cross-class` answer. `comparable` answers as before; `no-class` (file, list-or-object, formula) and `unjudged` return `undefined`; a side the object's field map does not carry returns `undefined`. The `addDays` arm is the old `offsetPairViolation` call, now one branch of an `offset !== undefined` ternary. Nothing wider than cross-class is refused. The three row-carried names `declaredReferenceNames` admits beyond the map (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) are judged only when the map carries them; by default it does, because the registry injects `AUDIT_FIELD_DEFS.created_at` / `updated_at` as `type: 'datetime'` (`registry.ts` near :655, `plan.audit`), so the datetime pair that matters is judged on an ordinary object.

2. **Refused set at `having` — right at this head, with one latent seam.** `assertConditionIsEvaluable` routes a reference with `addDays` to the unchanged offset rule and a plain one to `assertSameClassReference`, which asks the spec's verdict of each aggregated column's TYPE (`columnTypeMeta` over `aggregatedRowColumnTypes`): a day bucket is `date`, a coarser bucket `text`, count / count_distinct / sum / avg `number`, min / max the field's type. The spec classes each of those as the having vocabulary does; a `file`, `image`, `formula` or structured-JSON projection answers `no-class` and is not judged. Latent seam: `columnTypeMeta` passes no `multiple`, so a `multiple: true` select / radio / lookup / user projection would read as a scalar `text`. Unreachable at this head: the #20808 door refuses a groupBy on a multi-value field, and the spec's `min` / `max` rows admit only numeric, temporal and boolean types, so no such column exists in an aggregated row. Noted for #21299's enumeration pin; not a defect of this diff.

3. **TYPE rather than the having class at the `having` seam — right.** `classOfDeclaredType` lumps every non-numeric, non-boolean, non-temporal type into `text`, so judging by it would have refused a file-against-number pair under the cross-class sentence, the narrowing the dispatch forbade; the type lets the spec answer `no-class` for it. Nothing else `having` judges moves: `types` is a new optional `EvaluableScope` member read by exactly one new branch; the `addDays` branch is logically unchanged (`classes && addDays` became `addDays`, then `classes`); `assertHavingIsEvaluable` has one caller (`engine.ts` :17317), which now passes the fourth argument.

4. **Words — right.** `crossClassReason` is byte-identical to the sentence `offsetPairViolation` built before, which is `applyCrossFieldComparison`'s cross-class sentence with "is stored as" read as "is" (the #20127 convention for computed columns). The per-aggregation wire message gains "compared as the same type class", the clause `uncompilableFieldReferenceError`'s wire message carries; the fields, the operator and the reason stay withheld, and the logged diagnostic keeps `where`'s shape (Operator ... on field ... compares against another field ..., which cannot be evaluated here: reason). `having` names its own projection, as #20127 does, and `columnPairError` says "with addDays" only when the reference carries one.

5. **`AggregatedColumnClass` — right, and not a public-surface change.** It becomes an alias of `CrossFieldComparisonClass`: the same six literals, so every existing use type-checks unchanged. It is not published: neither the `.` nor the `./core` entry of `@objectstack/objectql` re-exports `having-filter.ts`; its consumers are two sibling door modules. The changeset's "No export or published type changes" is accurate.

6. **`addDays` pairs — unchanged, confirmed.** `offsetPairViolation` keeps its guards and its prose; the #20127 and #20148 pins are untouched except one `ANSWERED` label ("the rule is the offset's" became "one class on both sides", the true reason now). Green in `Test Core` on this head.

7. **Pins — they prove what they claim.** The objectql per-aggregation helper drives 8 cells (native-capable and raw driver, empty and populated, grouped and ungrouped) and asserts `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, zero `aggregate` / `find` calls, one message across cells and 8 logged diagnostics naming both fields and both classes; the `having` helper drives both doors, empty and populated, zero reads. The `packages/rest` pins drive `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query` on a real `SqlDriver` over better-sqlite3 with `closed_at` (datetime) added to the fixture, assert zero reads and the twin's 400, and parse the two class names and the trailing sentence out of the twin's own withheld diagnostic (`withheldFilterDiagnosticOf`, a published driver-sql export) before asserting them inside the per-aggregation log line and the `having` message. Same-class controls (5 per-aggregation, 3 having, 3 REST) and two registry-less controls answer as before. The ablation anchor (the `target === undefined || referent === undefined` guard replaced by an always-true return) disables `crossClassReferenceViolation` at both positions and nothing else; 7 + 9 objectql and 2 REST refusal blocks is exactly the count the diff adds, so "16 and 2 red, controls green" is the only outcome that mutation can produce. Not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

- `minor` with the BREAKING banner is right: ADR-0087's amendment of 2026-09-13 (#18003) states that pre-GA a metadata-facing break ships `minor`, carrying the BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition entry; `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major` until GA; the objectql CHANGELOG carries the same sentence on more than ten 17.6.0 entries.
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is a category `check-adr-0087-registration` lists (its `CATEGORIES`, :497) and re-verifies on every run; `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on this head. The claim holds on the diff: no spec key, export, stored shape or accepted request shape moves; what is refused is a comparison `where` already refuses, and which same-class column the author meant is not something a ledger entry can decide.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` stands at line start in the changeset (line 7) and in the PR body (line 3).
- Prose: accurate. "What was accepted before" is the card's two measured queries and the whole-day reading that answered them; "What is refused now" names the six scalar operators, the spec's six classes, both doors, 400 before any read on an empty set as on a populated one, and the withheld-versus-named split per position; the remedy is `where`'s (compare same-class columns); "Unchanged" correctly keeps same-class, `addDays`, no-declaration and no-class pairs out of this rule.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1 (`engine.ts`, one argument)** — recorded by amendment 5944487371 and stated in the PR body. Necessary for the no-narrowing constraint (judgment 3). Nit, not a contract issue: `aggregatedRowColumnTypes(query.groupBy, query.aggregations, declaredFields)` is now computed a third time inside `aggregate` (also :17349 and :17416) rather than hoisted beside `havingColumnClasses`.
- **Deviation 2 (`packages/rest` test)** — recorded by the amendment. Justified: `@objectstack/objectql` declares no `driver-sql` dependency (its package.json) and the engine refuses no `where` reference, so a twin cannot be refused inside objectql; the file is a test only, in the existing #20148 twin harness, with the fixture widened by one `datetime` column. The amendment says the cross-lane surface is declared on the `domain:cli` seat post; that post is outside this review's inputs and is taken as recorded.
- **Open question (refuse `no-class` too?)** — answered A and filed as #21299 (open, created 2026-10-02T02:30Z, unlabelled, awaiting triage). It names both positions, the `crossClassReferenceViolation` seam, the four measured pairs with their `where` twins, `applyInMemoryAggregation` as an enumerated position, and an enumeration pin over positions and verdicts. It covers the measured positions. Escalated to the seat for #21299's enumeration: add the no-declaration rows beside the four verdicts (the registry-less host, and the `declaredReferenceNames`-admitted row-carried columns on an object that opts out of audit fields) and the latent `columnTypeMeta` `multiple` seam of judgment 2.
- **Out-of-scope findings** — the `no-class` divergence is #21299's; `applyInMemoryAggregation` is enumerated on #21299 (no in-repo caller passes a per-aggregation reference there; `packages/verify` date-bucket parity is its only external caller); the 500-character truncation is `rest-server.ts` :11375 (`clientMsg.slice(0, 500)`), pre-existing, and the class reason sits in the first part of the `having` message, so the REST pin's asserted fragment survives it. All answered.
- **Downstream #21242 (`lteBound`)** — after this PR, on a registered object with its default system fields, no `having` or per-aggregation query reaches `lteBound` with a cross-class plain reference between two columns the field map declares: both positions refuse before any read, and `created_at` / `updated_at` sit in that map as `datetime`. What can still reach it, each by the dispatch's own no-declaration-not-judged direction, read and not measured: (a) a registry-less host, which this PR pins as answered, and those two controls encode `lteBound`'s whole-day answer (`picked: 3`; `['c1']`), so #21242 must expect them to move; (b) an object that opts out of audit fields, where `created_at` / `updated_at` pass `declaredReferenceNames` but have no map entry, while driver-sql refuses the `where` twin; (c) a direct `applyInMemoryAggregation` caller. None is a declared-column production path, so this card unblocks #21242 as far as its scope reaches; (a) and (b) go to the seat with #21299.
- **Check-runs on the head**, read 2026-10-02T02:53Z: 34 of 34 completed, 31 success and 3 skipped (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), none in progress; combined status success. The gate verdicts are green.
